title: Codespaces
text:
A GitHub Codespace is VS Code in your browser, already set up with R, Quarto, the tidyverse, tidymodels and medicaldata. All you need is a GitHub account.
This Codespace uses the same setup as the HDSx course book, whose pages walk through each step with screenshots:

title: Codespaces
text:
Check that it works
Once the Codespace is ready, open example.qmd and render it. It loads the course packages, draws three charts, and fits a small logistic regression. The rendered files go in the _site/ folder: click _site/example.html to open the page. It should match the Example page on this website.

title: My First Report
text:
Packages
Every package this report uses, loaded once at the top: the tidyverse for data and charts, tidymodels for modelling, and medicaldata for example datasets.

library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(medicaldata)

title: My First Report
section: A first look at the data
text:
A first look at the data
data/patients.csv is a small, made-up practice dataset of 12 synthetic patients, It comes from ehsanx/HDSx-workspace, The code chunk below reads it and shows the first few rows.

patients <- read.csv("data/patients.csv")
head(patients)

  id age sex region systolic_bp diabetes
1  1  54   F  North         128       no
2  2  61   M  North         141      yes
3  3  47   F  South         119       no
4  4  72   M   East         150      yes
5  5  38   F   West         112       no
6  6  59   M  South         134       no

title: My First Report
text:
A first chart

ggplot(patients, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Number of patients")

title: My First Report
text:
A second chart

ggplot(patients, aes(x = age, y = systolic_bp, colour = diabetes)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Systolic blood pressure (mm Hg)",
       colour = "Diabetes")

title: My First Report
text:
A medicaldata dataset
medicaldata has 15 medical datasets to explore, each described on the package website.






Note



The website also lists a few newer datasets that the installed version (0.2.0, from CRAN) doesn’t have yet: run data(package = "medicaldata") to see the ones you can load.
To get the newer datasets too, install the development version from GitHub in the R terminal, then restart R:

remotes::install_github("higgi13425/medicaldata")



covid_testing holds deidentified COVID-19 test results from 2020.

ggplot(covid_testing, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Number of tests")

title: MEDI 504A — Biostatistics with Tidyverse
text:
UBC MEDI 504A (Emerging Topics in Experimental Medicine), Winter 2026 term. Two sessions: tidy data as the foundation, then linear and logistic regression on medical data.
Course website: https://chendaniely.github.io/MEDI-504A-2026W1-biostats/



Lecture 1: Tidy data. Monday, Nov 2, 2026, 1:00–3:00 PM PST, ECC 100 LT. Start at Welcome.
Lecture 2: Modelling lab. Wednesday, Nov 4, 2026, 1:00–3:00 PM PST, DHCC 4223. Start at Clone the repository.

Work in a Codespace, with nothing to install, or on your own computer (local setup).




Timbers, T., Campbell, T., & Lee, M. Data Science: A First Introduction. https://datasciencebook.ca/
Chen, D. Data Science for the Biomedical Sciences. https://ds4biomed.tech/
Wickham, H., Çetinkaya-Rundel, M., & Grolemund, G. (2023). R for Data Science (2nd ed.). https://r4ds.hadley.nz/
Kuhn, M., & Silge, J. Tidy Modeling with R. https://www.tmwr.org/
Wickham, H. (2014). Tidy Data. Journal of Statistical Software, 59(10), 1–23. https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v059.i10




This repository is a Quarto website. .github/workflows/publish.yml renders it on every push to main and publishes it to GitHub Pages from the gh-pages branch. To preview it locally, run quarto preview.
Quarto extensions, committed in _extensions/:

coatless-quarto/embedio: embeds each Lecture 1 slide deck at the top of its page. Update it with quarto add coatless-quarto/embedio.

R

An editor
Use either of these:

Positron: https://positron.posit.co/
RStudio Desktop: https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/

text:
Quarto
Install Quarto to render the lecture documents: https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/.

text:
R packages
Run this once in the R console:
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "tidymodels", "medicaldata"))

text:
Git
You’ll clone the course repository in Lecture 2. Install Git by following Happy Git and GitHub for the useR: https://happygitwithr.com/install-git.html.
